statute_title: Operating Under the Influence of Intoxicating Liquor or Other Substance
elements: Defendant operated, attempted to operate, or was in actual physical control of a vehicle
On a highway
While under the influence of intoxicating liquor, a drug, or a combination
Or had a BAC of .08 or higher
mandatory_minimum: None (first); 60 consecutive hours or 200 hours community service (second); 96 consecutive hours (third); 192 consecutive hours (fourth+)
enhancements: Third offense within 20 years (felony, up to 5 years)
Fourth or subsequent within lifetime (felony, up to 10 years)
Refusal to submit to evidentiary test
notes: Vermont DUI penalties under § 1210. License suspension: 90 days (first), 18 months (second), lifetime (third). $50 surcharge on all DUI convictions. 20-year lookback period for prior offenses.

elements: Defendant operated a vehicle on a highway
While under the influence of alcohol or drugs
BAC .08 or higher, or impairment of driving ability
No prior DUI convictions within 20 years
notes: 90-day license suspension. Eligible for ignition interlock restricted license. Alcohol/drug screening and treatment may be ordered. $50 surcharge assessed.

penalty_min: 60 consecutive hours or 200 hours community service (second); 96 hours (third); 192 hours (fourth+)
elements: Defendant operated a vehicle on a highway while under the influence
One or more prior DUI convictions within 20 years (second); two or more (third); three or more (fourth+)
mandatory_minimum: 60 consecutive hours imprisonment or 200 hours community service (second); 96 consecutive hours (third); 192 consecutive hours (fourth+)
notes: Second: 18-month license suspension. Third: lifetime revocation. Fourth+: lifetime revocation. Ignition interlock required for license reinstatement.

offense_class: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
penalty_min: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
penalty_max: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
fine_max: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
elements: Defendant operated a vehicle on a highway
While under the influence of any drug or combination of alcohol and any drug
To a degree that renders the defendant incapable of driving safely
mandatory_minimum: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
enhancements: Combined influence of alcohol and drugs
notes: No per se limit for drugs. Prosecution must prove actual impairment. Drug Recognition Expert (DRE) evaluation commonly used.

statute_title: Negligent Driving with Serious Bodily Injury or Death
elements: Defendant drove a vehicle on a highway
In a manner that created an unjustifiable risk to persons or property
notes: Vermont does not have a standalone 'reckless driving' statute like most states. Negligent operation (23 V.S.A. § 1091) and careless/negligent driving (§ 1038) cover similar conduct.

statute_title: Leaving Scene of Accident — Injury or Death
elements: Defendant was the operator of a vehicle involved in an accident
Accident resulted in injury, death, or property damage
Defendant failed to stop at the scene
Defendant failed to provide identification and render reasonable assistance
notes: Leaving the scene of a fatal accident carries up to 15 years. Leaving the scene of an accident with injury carries up to 5 years.

statute_title: Vehicular Homicide / Grossly Negligent Operation Resulting in Death
elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle
In a grossly negligent manner or while under the influence
Caused the death of another person
notes: Vermont does not have a specific vehicular homicide statute. Deaths caused by negligent driving may be charged under the general manslaughter statute (13 V.S.A. § 2304) or grossly negligent operation (23 V.S.A. § 1091).

elements: Defendant caused the death of another person
Through culpable negligence
While operating a motor vehicle
notes: Vermont charges vehicular deaths under the general manslaughter statute. Involuntary manslaughter covers unintentional killings from culpable negligence.

statute_title: Driving While License Suspended or Revoked
elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle on a highway
While the defendant's license was suspended or revoked
Defendant had knowledge of the suspension or revocation
notes: Penalties differ based on whether the underlying suspension was criminal (DUI) or civil. Criminal suspension violations carry harsher penalties.

offense_class: Misdemeanor; Felony if creating risk of death or serious bodily injury
elements: Defendant was operating a motor vehicle
A law enforcement officer signaled the defendant to stop
Defendant willfully attempted to elude the officer by driving recklessly
enhancements: Creating risk of death or serious bodily injury (felony)
notes: Eluding an officer while creating a risk of serious harm is a felony.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (most drugs in small amounts); Felony (larger amounts or Schedule I/II)
elements: Defendant knowingly and unlawfully possessed a regulated drug
Without a valid prescription or authorization
notes: Vermont classifies drugs as 'regulated drugs' under Title 18. Penalties vary significantly by substance and amount.

offense_class: Civil violation (1 oz or less for 21+); Misdemeanor (over 1 oz); Felony (over 2 oz)
penalty_max: Civil fine (1 oz or less); 6 months (1-2 oz); 3 years (2 oz to 1 lb); 5 years (1-10 lbs); 15 years (10+ lbs)
elements: Defendant possessed marijuana
Amount determines classification
notes: Vermont legalized recreational marijuana for adults 21+ in 2018 (up to 1 oz possession). Retail sales began in 2022. Possession over 1 oz remains criminal.

penalty_max: 1 year (under 2.5 grams); 5 years (2.5+ grams); 10 years (1+ oz); 20 years (2.5+ oz)
elements: Defendant knowingly and unlawfully possessed cocaine
Amount determines classification
notes: Cocaine is classified as a narcotic. Penalties escalate sharply with quantity.

elements: Defendant knowingly and unlawfully possessed methamphetamine
Amount determines classification
notes: Methamphetamine is a growing concern in Vermont. Possession penalties parallel other regulated drugs.

statute_title: Sale or Dispensing of Regulated Drug
offense_class: Felony; varies by substance and amount
penalty_max: 5 years to 30 years depending on substance and amount
fine_max: $100,000 to $1,000,000 depending on substance and amount
elements: Defendant sold, dispensed, or possessed with intent to sell a regulated drug
Classification depends on substance and amount
notes: Penalties vary greatly by substance. Heroin trafficking (§ 4233) carries the most severe penalties. Each substance has its own statutory section.

penalty_max: 10 years (under 2.5 grams); 20 years (2.5+ grams); 30 years (1+ oz)
elements: Defendant sold or dispensed cocaine
Or possessed cocaine with intent to sell or dispense
notes: Each regulated drug has its own distribution statute section. Cocaine distribution penalties are among the most severe.

elements: Defendant manufactured, compounded, processed, or prepared a regulated drug
enhancements: Manufacturing in presence of a child
notes: Manufacturing penalties vary by substance. Methamphetamine lab cleanup liability may also apply.

elements: Defendant possessed drug paraphernalia
With the intent to use it to introduce a controlled substance into the body
notes: Delivery of paraphernalia to a minor carries enhanced penalties.

statute_title: Possession with Intent to Sell or Dispense
offense_class: Felony; varies by substance and amount
penalty_max: Varies by substance and amount (5-30 years)
elements: Defendant possessed a regulated drug
With intent to sell or dispense
Intent inferred from quantity, packaging, scales, cash, or other circumstances
notes: Intent to distribute typically inferred from large quantities, packaging materials, scales, large amounts of cash, and communications.

elements: Defendant caused the death of another person
With willful, deliberate, and premeditated killing
Or during the perpetration of arson, sexual assault, aggravated sexual assault, kidnapping, robbery, or burglary
notes: Vermont abolished the death penalty in 1972. First-degree murder carries a mandatory minimum of 35 years to life.

elements: Defendant caused the death of another person
With malice aforethought
But without premeditation and deliberation
notes: Second-degree murder carries a mandatory minimum of 20 years to life. All murders not classified as first-degree are second-degree.

elements: Defendant caused the death of another person
In the heat of passion on sudden provocation
Or under circumstances that would cause a reasonable person to lose self-control
notes: Manslaughter is a general felony carrying up to 15 years. Heat of passion is the typical basis for voluntary manslaughter.

elements: Defendant caused the death of another person
Through culpable negligence or recklessness
Without intent to kill
notes: Vermont has a single manslaughter statute covering both voluntary and involuntary manslaughter. Up to 15 years imprisonment.

elements: Defendant attempted to cause or caused serious bodily injury to another
Or caused bodily injury to another with a deadly weapon
Under circumstances manifesting extreme indifference to human life
notes: Aggravated assault is a felony carrying up to 15 years and $10,000 fine.

elements: Defendant attempted to cause or recklessly caused bodily injury to another
Or negligently caused bodily injury to another with a deadly weapon
Or attempted by physical menace to put another in fear of imminent serious bodily injury
notes: Simple assault is a misdemeanor. Enhanced if against law enforcement or other protected persons.

elements: Defendant intentionally caused bodily injury to another person
notes: Vermont combines assault and battery under the simple assault statute. No separate battery offense.

elements: Defendant assaulted another person
And robbed, stole, or took from that person money, goods, or other property
enhancements: Armed with a dangerous weapon (minimum 1 year, maximum 15 years)
Bodily injury caused (minimum 1 year, maximum 20 years)
notes: Simple robbery carries up to 10 years. Armed robbery carries 1-15 years. Robbery causing bodily injury carries 1-20 years.

elements: Defendant committed assault and robbery
While armed with a dangerous weapon
notes: Armed robbery carries a mandatory minimum of 1 year and maximum of 15 years. If bodily injury is caused, maximum increases to 20 years.

elements: Defendant knowingly restrained another person
With intent to hold for ransom, use as a shield, accomplish a felony, inflict bodily injury, or terrorize
notes: Kidnapping carries up to life imprisonment and $50,000 fine. Unlawful restraint (§ 2406) is a lesser included offense.

penalty_max: Life imprisonment (death resulting); 20 years (occupied building); 10 years (other property)
elements: Defendant willfully and maliciously set fire to or burned a building, structure, or property
notes: Arson causing death carries up to life (§ 501). Arson of a dwelling or occupied structure (§ 502) up to 20 years. Arson of other property (§ 503) up to 10 years.

elements: Defendant intended to commit murder
Defendant engaged in conduct constituting a substantial step toward commission
The victim survived
notes: Attempted murder carries significant penalties. Vermont's attempt statute provides for punishment proportional to the completed offense.

statute_title: Aggravated Assault with a Deadly Weapon
elements: Defendant caused bodily injury to another
With a deadly weapon
notes: Assault with a deadly weapon falls under the aggravated assault statute. A deadly weapon includes firearms, knives, and other instruments capable of causing death or serious bodily harm.

penalty_max: 10 years (grand larceny); 6 months or less (petit larceny)
elements: Defendant stole from the person of another or property valued at more than $900
With intent to permanently deprive the owner
enhancements: Theft from a person (grand larceny regardless of amount)
notes: Vermont uses traditional larceny terminology. Grand larceny threshold is $900. Theft from a person is always grand larceny.

elements: Defendant stole property valued at more than $900
Or stole from the person of another regardless of value
With intent to permanently deprive the owner
notes: Grand larceny is a felony carrying up to 10 years imprisonment and $5,000 fine.

elements: Defendant stole property valued at $900 or less
With intent to permanently deprive the owner
enhancements: Third or subsequent offense (up to 3 years)
notes: Petit larceny is a misdemeanor. Third offense becomes punishable by up to 3 years.

elements: Defendant concealed upon their person or otherwise removed merchandise from a retail establishment
With intent to deprive the merchant of the merchandise without paying
notes: Penalties follow the larceny thresholds. Civil liability to the merchant also applies.

elements: Defendant entered any building or structure
Without the owner's consent or lawful authority
With the intent to commit a felony, petit larceny, or simple assault
notes: Burglary in Vermont carries up to 15 years. Entry during nighttime or into an occupied dwelling may result in harsher sentencing.

elements: Defendant entered an occupied dwelling
Without the owner's consent
With intent to commit a felony, petit larceny, or simple assault
While a person was present in the dwelling
notes: Burglary of an occupied dwelling while armed or causing bodily injury carries enhanced penalties up to 25 years.

elements: Defendant stole a motor vehicle belonging to another
With intent to permanently deprive the owner
notes: Most vehicles exceed the $900 grand larceny threshold. Also see unauthorized use of a motor vehicle.

offense_class: Same as the larceny classification based on value
elements: Defendant bought, received, or concealed stolen property
Knowing or having reason to know the property was stolen
notes: Penalties mirror larceny classifications based on value of stolen property.

elements: Defendant intentionally damaged property of another
Without the owner's consent
notes: Unlawful mischief is Vermont's primary property destruction statute. Restitution typically ordered.

elements: Defendant entered or remained on land of another
Without the owner's consent
After being warned by the owner or by posted signs
notes: Unlawful trespass on posted land. Enhanced penalties for trespass on certain protected properties.

elements: Defendant intentionally or recklessly damaged tangible property of another
notes: Vermont uses 'unlawful mischief' rather than 'criminal mischief.' Same statute as vandalism.

elements: Defendant committed an assault against a family or household member
notes: Family or household member includes current/former spouse, cohabitant, person related by blood or marriage, persons with shared child, or dating relationship.

elements: Defendant intentionally caused bodily injury to a family or household member
notes: Vermont combines assault and battery under the domestic assault statute.

statute_title: Cruelty to Children under 10 by One over 16
elements: Defendant, being over 16 years of age
Willfully assaulted, ill-treated, or caused injury to a child under 10
Or willfully endangered the health or life of a child under 10
notes: Mandatory reporting. DUI with child in vehicle may trigger separate endangerment charges.

elements: Defendant willfully assaulted, ill-treated, neglected, or abandoned a child
Causing or permitting physical injury, emotional injury, or impairment
notes: Child abuse resulting in death may be charged as homicide.

elements: A valid abuse prevention order was in effect
Defendant had knowledge of the order
Defendant willfully violated the terms of the order
notes: Violation of an abuse prevention order is a separate criminal offense.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (first); Felony (second+ or with threat of death/serious injury)
elements: Defendant purposely engaged in a course of conduct directed at a specific person
That would cause a reasonable person to fear for their safety or the safety of another closely connected person
enhancements: Threat of death or serious bodily injury
notes: Includes electronic/cyber stalking. Stalking orders available.

statute_title: Disturbing Peace by Use of Telephone or Other Electronic Communication
elements: Defendant, with intent to terrify, intimidate, threaten, harass, or annoy
Made telephone calls or electronic communications
notes: Covers harassment by telephone, text, email, and other electronic means.

statute_title: Abuse, Neglect, or Exploitation of Vulnerable Adult
elements: Defendant abused, neglected, or exploited a vulnerable adult
Vulnerable adult includes persons 60+ or disabled adults
notes: Mandatory reporting required. Financial exploitation is prosecuted based on amount.

statute_title: Carrying a Dangerous Weapon While Committing a Crime
penalty_max: Additional term of imprisonment up to 5 years
elements: Defendant carried a dangerous or deadly weapon while committing a felony
notes: Vermont has very permissive gun laws — no permit required for open or concealed carry. This statute adds penalties when weapons are used during crime commission.

statute_title: Possession of Firearms by Convicted Felons
elements: Defendant possessed, owned, or had custody of a firearm
Defendant had been convicted of a violent crime as defined
notes: Applies only to persons convicted of certain violent crimes. Vermont is one of the most permissive states for gun ownership but restricts violent felons.

statute_title: Possession of Dangerous Weapon in Court or State Building
elements: Defendant carried a weapon into a courthouse or state building
Where weapons are prohibited
notes: Vermont allows permit-less open and concealed carry. Location restrictions apply to courthouses and certain government buildings.

elements: Defendant recklessly discharged a firearm
Creating a risk of harm to persons
notes: Reckless endangerment with a firearm is a felony. General reckless endangerment is a separate misdemeanor.

elements: Defendant obtained personal identifying information of another
Without the other person's consent
And used the information to obtain money, credit, goods, services, or anything of value
notes: Identity theft is a felony carrying up to 10 years and $10,000 fine.

elements: Defendant was entrusted with property of another
Defendant embezzled or fraudulently converted the property to their own use
notes: Vermont has a specific embezzlement statute separate from larceny.

elements: Defendant forged, counterfeited, or falsely altered any writing
With intent to defraud
notes: Forgery is a felony carrying up to 10 years.

elements: Defendant forged, counterfeited, or falsely altered any coin, note, or bill
With intent to defraud
notes: Counterfeiting is prosecuted under the forgery statute. Federal charges may also apply.

elements: Defendant issued a check or draft
Knowing there were insufficient funds
With intent to defraud
notes: Presumption of knowledge and intent if check not made good within 10 days of notice.

elements: Defendant knowingly presented false information in connection with an insurance claim
With intent to defraud an insurer
notes: Includes all types of insurance fraud. Restitution may also be ordered.

elements: Defendant used a credit or debit card
Knowing it was stolen, forged, expired, revoked, or not theirs
With intent to defraud
notes: Penalties follow the larceny thresholds based on amount obtained.

elements: Defendant conducted or attempted to conduct a financial transaction
Knowing the property was derived from unlawful activity
With intent to promote unlawful activity or conceal the source
notes: Also subject to federal prosecution under 18 U.S.C. § 1956.

elements: Defendant obtained money, property, or services by false pretenses
Defendant knowingly made false representations
With intent to defraud
notes: General fraud prosecuted under the false pretenses statute.

elements: Defendant engaged in a sexual act with another person
Without the consent of the other person
Or through compulsion, coercion, or by placing the other person in fear
notes: Sexual assault carries up to 20 years. Aggravated sexual assault (§ 3253) carries life. Vermont uses 'sexual assault' rather than 'rape.'

elements: Defendant committed sexual assault as defined in § 3252
And caused serious bodily injury
Or was armed with a deadly weapon
Or the victim had not reached their 13th birthday
notes: Aggravated sexual assault carries a mandatory minimum of 10 years and maximum of life. Lifetime sex offender registration required.

offense_class: Felony (lewd and lascivious conduct with child); Misdemeanor (general open lewdness)
elements: Defendant willfully and lewdly exposed their body in a public place
Or committed a lewd or lascivious act
notes: Open and gross lewdness is a misdemeanor. Lewd and lascivious conduct with a child is a felony.

elements: Defendant solicited or paid for sexual conduct
notes: Vermont treats solicitation as a misdemeanor. Solicitation of a minor carries felony penalties.

elements: Defendant knowingly possessed, produced, or distributed a visual depiction of a child engaged in sexually explicit conduct
notes: Federal charges commonly also apply. Sex offender registration required.

statute_title: Failure to Register as Sex Offender
elements: Defendant was required to register as a sex offender
Defendant knowingly failed to register, verify, or update registration information
notes: Vermont Sex Offender Registry requires registration for 10 years or lifetime depending on the offense.

statute_title: Sexual Assault — Victim Under Age of Consent
elements: Defendant engaged in a sexual act with a person
Who was under the age of 16
Regardless of consent
enhancements: Victim under 13 (aggravated sexual assault, 10 years to life)
notes: Age of consent in Vermont is 16. Sexual acts with persons under 16 are sexual assault regardless of consent. Under 13 triggers aggravated sexual assault charges.

elements: Defendant, with intent to cause public inconvenience or alarm
Engaged in fighting, violent, or threatening behavior
Or made unreasonable noise or offensive, obscene, or abusive language in a public place
notes: Common low-level offense.

elements: Defendant intentionally resisted a lawful arrest
By using physical force or physical interference
notes: Applies to physical resistance. Passive non-compliance alone may not constitute this offense.

offense_class: Misdemeanor; Felony (aiding escape or harboring felon)
elements: Defendant intentionally obstructed, impeded, or hindered the administration of justice
Or prevented the apprehension of a person known to have committed a crime
enhancements: Aiding escape or harboring a felon
notes: Includes providing false information, concealing evidence, harboring suspects, and interfering with investigations.

offense_class: Punishable by fine and/or imprisonment at the court's discretion
elements: Defendant willfully disobeyed a court order
Or engaged in disorderly conduct in the court's presence
notes: Courts have inherent contempt power for both civil and criminal contempt.

elements: Defendant appeared in a public place while intoxicated
And engaged in conduct that caused public inconvenience or alarm
notes: Vermont addresses public intoxication through the disorderly conduct statute. Protective custody may be used as an alternative to arrest.

elements: Defendant was released on bail or conditions of release
Defendant failed to appear in court as required
notes: Failure to appear is a separate offense. Bond forfeiture and bench warrant may be issued.

elements: Defendant knowingly filed a false report
With a law enforcement agency
Claiming a crime had been committed
notes: Filing a false report is a misdemeanor.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (first); Felony (with weapon or bodily injury threat)
elements: Defendant, by words or conduct, knowingly
Threatened to use a deadly weapon against another
Or threatened to cause bodily injury to another
And the threat was made under circumstances which would reasonably cause apprehension
notes: Criminal threatening with a deadly weapon is a felony carrying up to 7 years.

elements: Defendant made a false statement under oath or affirmation
In a judicial proceeding
The statement was material
Defendant knew the statement was false
notes: Perjury is a felony carrying up to 15 years in Vermont.

elements: Defendant offered, gave, or promised anything of value
To a public official
With intent to influence the official's vote, opinion, judgment, or action
notes: Both the person offering and the official accepting may be charged.

elements: Defendant was in lawful custody or confinement
Defendant escaped or attempted to escape
notes: Sentence runs consecutively to any existing sentence.

elements: Defendant cruelly treated, neglected, or abandoned an animal
Or intentionally caused unnecessary pain or suffering
notes: Aggravated cruelty to animals is a felony. Includes animal fighting under § 352a.

penalty_max: Up to the maximum sentence for the original offense
fine_max: Up to the maximum fine for the original offense
elements: Defendant was placed on probation
Defendant violated one or more conditions of probation
notes: Court may revoke probation and impose any sentence originally available. Graduated sanctions may be used.

elements: Defendant was released on parole
Defendant violated one or more conditions of parole
notes: Parole Board makes revocation decisions.

statute_title: Accessory — Aiding in Commission of Felony
elements: A crime was committed by another person
Defendant aided in the commission of the felony
Defendant was present at the commission or aided before or during
notes: Persons who aid in the commission of a felony are punishable as principal offenders.

offense_class: Punished as the completed offense would be, or as otherwise specifically provided
elements: Defendant intended to commit a specific offense
Defendant did an act toward the commission thereof
The act went beyond mere preparation
notes: Vermont's attempt statute provides that an attempt may be punished as the completed offense unless otherwise provided by law.

offense_class: Misdemeanor; Felony if target offense is a felony and an overt act is committed
elements: Defendant agreed with one or more persons to commit a criminal offense
An overt act was committed in furtherance of the conspiracy
notes: Conspiracy requires an agreement and an overt act. Penalties depend on the target offense.
